subtopics.title: Global Relations and Forums
subtopics.summary: India deepened ties with Brazil, Israel and Finland through trade, defence, technology and workforce arrangements. Brazil's state visit set a US$30 billion bilateral trade target for 2030. The Takeshima/Dokdo islets dispute between Japan and South Korea remains a sovereignty issue rooted in Japan's colonial rule over Korea.
facts: Brazil-India Strategic Partnership dates to 2006; diplomatic relations were established in 1948.
Bilateral trade target is US$30 billion by 2030; trade had reached US$15.21 billion in 2025.
India and Brazil signed a Critical Minerals MoU covering rare earths, lithium, graphite, niobium and nickel.
Embraer will set up an E175 jet assembly line with Adani Defence and Aerospace.
Validity of multiple-entry tourist and business visas was extended from 5 years to 10 years.
India and Israel upgraded ties to a Special Strategic Partnership for Peace, Innovation and Prosperity.
Israel will allow up to 50,000 Indian workers over the next 5 years.
Israel is India's 2nd largest trading partner in Asia; bilateral trade was US$3.75 billion in FY 2024-25.
Takeshima (Japan) and Dokdo (South Korea) are islets in the Sea of Japan; the 1951 San Francisco Peace Treaty did not name them explicitly.
India and Finland elevated ties to a Strategic Partnership in digitalisation and sustainability; both aim to double bilateral trade by 2030.

subtopics.title: Constitution, Law and Governance
subtopics.summary: The removal of a Chief Election Commissioner follows a special parliamentary process modelled on the removal of a Supreme Court judge, and no CEC has ever been removed. The Supreme Court recognises passive euthanasia under strict medical and judicial safeguards. Ladakh's demands for statehood and Sixth Schedule status, and the government's online takedown powers, are also in focus.
facts: Opposition parties moved a removal motion against CEC Gyanesh Kumar; no CEC has ever been removed in India.
Under Article 324(5), the CEC can be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge.
The CEC can be removed only on two grounds: proven misbehaviour and incapacity.
A removal motion needs support of 100 Lok Sabha members or 50 Rajya Sabha members to be introduced.
Both Houses must pass the motion with a majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting, in the same session.
Other Election Commissioners are removed by the President on the CEC's recommendation; Parliament is not involved.
Ladakh has been a Union Territory without a legislature since 2019 and has only one Lok Sabha seat.
Ladakh demands include Sixth Schedule inclusion, full statehood, a separate Public Service Commission and two Lok Sabha seats (Leh and Kargil).
Common Cause v. Union of India (2018) legalised passive euthanasia and recognised living wills; active euthanasia remains illegal.
Section 69A allows centralised blocking of online content, while Section 79(3)(b) allows direct takedown requests via the Sahyog Portal.

subtopics.title: Public Health, Water and Environment
subtopics.summary: The Universal Immunisation Programme and Mission Indradhanush aim to protect children and pregnant women against vaccine-preventable diseases. Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 extends rural tap water coverage to December 2028 with a focus on service delivery. India's biodiversity commitments under the CBD and the Nagoya Protocol centre on benefit-sharing and national reporting.
facts: The Universal Immunisation Programme is one of the largest public immunisation programmes in the world and was re-launched in 1985.
Mission Indradhanush was launched on 25 December 2014 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Intensified Mission Indradhanush 2.0 (December 2019) targeted districts with 70% or below immunisation coverage.
India was certified polio-free in 2014; National Vaccination Day is observed on 16 March.
U-WIN is a digital platform to track vaccination records.
Jal Jeevan Mission was launched in 2019 under the Ministry of Jal Shakti with a standard of 55 litres per capita per day.
Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 is extended to December 2028 and aims at tap connections for all 19.36 crore rural households.
Jal Arpan introduces a formal handover protocol involving Gram Panchayats and Village Water Committees (Paani Samitis).
The Nagoya Protocol was adopted in 2010 at Nagoya (Japan) and entered into force in 2014.
Out of 23 KMGBF targets, only 2 are on track for achievement by 2030; India hosts 98 Ramsar sites.

subtopics.title: Economy, Security and Science
subtopics.summary: India's forex reserves fell by US$7.052 billion, driven by dollar strength, RBI intervention and higher crude oil prices. The PRAHAAR framework sets out seven pillars of India's zero-tolerance counter-terror doctrine. Defence and navigation updates include Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station in eastern Ladakh and the NavIC satellite system.
facts: India opposed including the IFD Agreement in the WTO framework; it is a plurilateral agreement binding only on signatories and based on the MFN principle.
Forex reserves dropped by US$7.052 billion to US$709.759 billion; they are held by the Reserve Bank of India.
Foreign currency assets are the largest component of forex reserves, followed by gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position.
NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2026 covers FY 2023-24 and relies on audited data from the CAG.
Odisha retained the top position among major states for the second consecutive year.
PRAHAAR is India's first comprehensive National Counter-Terrorism Policy Framework, institutionalising a zero-tolerance doctrine.
PRAHAAR's seven pillars cover prevention, responses, aggregating internal synergy, human rights, attenuating radicalisation, aligning global cooperation and recovery.
Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station was built in 1962 at an elevation of 13,700 feet in Changthang, about 25 km from the LAC.
NavIC is India's indigenous regional navigation system developed by ISRO and needs at least 4 operational satellites.
Atomic clock failure on IRNSS-1F weakened NavIC, as functional satellites dropped from 4 to 3.

subtopics.title: History and Personalities
subtopics.summary: Shaheed Diwas recalls Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Shivaram Hari Rajguru, who were linked to the Lahore Conspiracy Case. The Dandi March of 1930 marked the formal launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement through defiance of the salt law. C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) and the ASMITA Athletics League complete this section.
facts: Shaheed Diwas is observed on 23 March; India also observes Martyrs' Day on 30 January.
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were executed in 1931 at the Lahore Central Jail.
Bhagat Singh founded the Naujawan Bharat Sabha in 1926; the HSRA was formed in 1928.
In the Lahore Conspiracy Case, Lala Lajpat Rai was fatally injured in a 1928 lathi charge during protest against the Simon Commission.
The Central Assembly Bombing of 1929 was carried out by Bhagat Singh with Batukeshwar Dutt.
The Dandi March started on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram and ended on 6 April 1930 at Dandi in Gujarat.
The Salt Act of 1882 gave the British colonial government exclusive control over salt production and distribution.
Rajaji was born on 10 December 1878 at Thorapalli (Tamil Nadu) and proposed the C.R. Formula in 1944.
Rajaji was the only Indian and the last Governor-General of India, serving from 1948 to 1950.
The ASMITA Athletics League was launched across 250 locations to promote women's participation in sports.

quizzes.passage: India's relations with partners across several continents moved forward in early 2026 through state visits, new agreements and participation in global forums. The most prominent visit was the state visit of the President of Brazil, which followed the Prime Minister's trip to Brazil in July 2025. The two countries reaffirmed their long-standing strategic partnership and agreed to deepen cooperation in trade, the digital economy and strategic sectors. Trade was another focus, and both sides set a long-term bilateral trade goal for the end of this decade. A joint declaration on digital partnership was adopted, covering digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. Their talks also covered energy transition and climate change, and the Prime Minister commended Brazil for hosting a major climate conference. Defence and space cooperation also featured in the discussions, which covered shared technology and innovation priorities. Relations with Israel were raised to a special strategic partnership level, reflecting closer cooperation in defence, technology and innovation. Separately, India and Finland agreed to elevate ties during a visit linked to the Raisina Dialogue, a forum launched in 2016 that discusses global governance, security and economics. Finally, the Takeshima and Dokdo islets remain a sovereignty dispute between Japan and South Korea, which protested a Japanese government-backed event in Shimane Prefecture.

quizzes.passage: India's diplomacy in early 2026 combined high-level visits with agreements on trade, technology and workforce mobility. The President of Brazil made a state visit to India, and the two countries adopted a joint declaration on digital partnership covering digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. The visit was accompanied by several sector agreements. Brazil's President also received an invitation to the BRICS 2026 Summit in India. Their strategic partnership dates back to 2006, and the two sides also discussed critical minerals, defence and food security. Ties with Israel were upgraded to a special strategic partnership, with new cooperation in cybersecurity, semiconductors and space technology. The Israel arrangements also addressed labour mobility over the coming years. In Europe, India and Finland agreed to elevate their relationship in digitalisation and sustainability during a visit linked to the Raisina Dialogue, a forum launched in 2016. Japan and South Korea continue to dispute a pair of islets that Japan calls Takeshima and South Korea calls Dokdo. The dispute is rooted in Japan's colonial rule over Korea, and the islets were not explicitly named in a 1951 peace treaty. Both countries describe the islets with names that reflect their sovereignty claims, which makes the matter politically sensitive. South Korea has protested a Japanese government-backed event held in Shimane Prefecture.

quizzes.passage: Health and water programmes in India have increasingly focused on delivery to citizens. The Universal Immunisation Programme is among the largest public immunisation efforts in the world, and it provides free vaccines to infants, children and pregnant women. Intensified drives have targeted areas where immunisation coverage was low, and a later round focused on children and pregnant women who missed doses during the Covid-19 pandemic. Digital tracking of vaccination records is also supported, and the programme aims to reduce child mortality, morbidity and disability. Vaccination drives are planned for children up to two years of age. On water, the Jal Jeevan Mission was extended to the end of 2028 with a shift from building infrastructure to citizen-centric service delivery. Under the extension, the government aims to provide functional household tap connections to all rural households. Water supply systems will also receive unique service area identifiers, which will help track water supply and service delivery. The mission's standards also emphasise community ownership, transparency and accountability. On the environment side, India reports its biodiversity commitments under the Convention on Biological Diversity, and the Nagoya Protocol governs access and benefit-sharing for genetic resources. Reports to the convention are periodic, and each signatory must describe the measures it takes to implement the treaty.

quizzes.passage: India's public health and water programmes have been revised to focus on regular delivery and sustained coverage. The Universal Immunisation Programme was re-launched in 1985 and offers free vaccines to infants and pregnant women against several vaccine-preventable diseases. Intensified drives have targeted districts where coverage is 70% or below, and a later drive reached children who missed doses during the Covid-19 pandemic. Mission Indradhanush aims to give full immunisation to children up to two years of age, and it is supported by a digital platform. Water policy has moved in a similar direction. The Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 extends work to December 2028, with its focus on citizen-centric service delivery rather than infrastructure alone. Under the Jal Arpan initiative, completed water infrastructure is handed over through a formal protocol involving Gram Panchayats. India's biodiversity commitments run alongside this, and the Convention on Biological Diversity requires member countries to submit periodic reports on the measures they take. India has also submitted its first national report under the Nagoya Protocol, which covers access and benefit-sharing mechanisms. The reports highlight progress in conservation, sustainable resource use and fair sharing of benefits from biological resources. Monetary and non-monetary benefits both count under this framework. Such progress is reported at regular intervals.

quizzes.passage: India's economic and security agenda in early 2026 touched on trade rules, reserve management, state finances, counter-terrorism, border infrastructure and satellite navigation. At the World Trade Organization, India opposed bringing an investment-related framework into the main trade system, even though many members supported it. Currency markets also drew attention, as India's foreign exchange reserves fell during the period. The reserves are held by the Reserve Bank of India, which uses them to stabilise the rupee and cushion external shocks. The reserves are governed by the Reserve Bank of India Act and the Foreign Exchange Management Act. Gold, special drawing rights and the reserve tranche position with the IMF are also part of the reserves. The central bank sold dollars at times to manage volatility. On state finances, NITI Aayog released an annual fiscal health evaluation that benchmarks states on quality of expenditure, revenue mobilisation and debt. The index covers major states and north-eastern and Himalayan states, which are ranked separately. In security, the government released a national counter-terrorism policy that promises a zero-tolerance approach. In eastern Ladakh, an airfield drew attention for strengthening India's presence near the border. Satellite navigation also drew attention after a clock failure on one satellite weakened a regional system.

quizzes.passage: Several economic and strategic developments in early 2026 reflected pressures in global markets and regional security. India's foreign exchange reserves declined by a notable amount, as the central bank supported the rupee and rising crude oil prices added to demand for dollars. The Reserve Bank of India manages these reserves, which consist of foreign currency assets, gold, special drawing rights and a reserve tranche position with the International Monetary Fund. An international framework on investment facilitation was discussed at the World Trade Organization, and India did not support it. In the same period, NITI Aayog released the Fiscal Health Index, an annual evaluation of states that relies on audited data from the Comptroller and Auditor General. On security, the government's counter-terrorism policy set out a zero-tolerance doctrine. Meanwhile, an airfield in eastern Ladakh drew attention for its high altitude and its proximity to the border. Satellite navigation was also in focus after an atomic clock failure affected a regional navigation system called NavIC, which is developed by ISRO and needs several satellites to work reliably. India's reserve tranche position is a quota-based reserve with the IMF. The reserves are used to stabilise the rupee, finance imports, cushion external shocks and enhance economic credibility.
